 The Sunscreen You Can Buy In The U.S. Just Got A LOT Better — Here's Why Derms Love It
 HuffPost Follow Tessa Flores Updated Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Updated Wed, October 21, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC Bemotrizinol sunscreens are now officially available in the U.S. Amazon Countless dermatologists will tell you sun protection is a non-negotiable in any skin care routine, and it's your best defense against skin cancer and premature skin aging. Despite the essentialism of sunscreen , the U.S. Food and Drug Administration hasn't approved new sunscreen filters on the American market in 25 years, while places like Asia, Europe and Australia have been far more innovative and exploratory in this sun protection arena. But that all ended this year, when bemotrizinol — also known as BEMT and sometimes seen on labels as Tinosorb S — finally got the green light in the US.
 "What makes it exciting is how much it does in a single ingredient," said Dr. Christina Marcelus , a New York-based board-certified dermatologist. She explained that bemotrizinol is part of the "chemical" sun filter class, which, unlike "physical" sunscreens, works by absorbing UV rays and turning them into a small amount of harmless heat. ("Physical" or "mineral" sunscreens that contain zinc oxide and titanium dioxide simply sit on top of your skin and — you guessed it — create a physical barrier against ultraviolet light.)
 "Most of the chemical filters we've had in the US cover either UVA or UVB, so you have to blend a few of them to get true broad-spectrum protection. Bemotrizinol covers the whole range on its own," Marcelus said. (FYI: UVA and UVB are simply two different types of rays.)
 Advertisement Advertisement Board-certified dermatologist Dr. Tiffany Clay-Ramsey said that bemotrizinol is also more photo-stable than previously available sun filters, so it doesn't break down in sunlight like most other chemical sunscreens. "This means you don't have to reapply it as often," she said.
 And we've likely all fallen victim to a sunscreen that claims to be completely white cast-free, only to still detect a chalky tinge left on the skin and a heavy finish that makes it unpleasant to wear.
 "Because [bemotrizinol] is a large, oil-loving molecule, it mostly stays on the surface of your skin instead of soaking in, and it blends into lightweight, non-greasy formulas with no white cast," Marcelus said.
 According to Marcelus, you can also expect these new sunscreen formulas to be lighter, gentler and non-comedogenic.
 Advertisement Advertisement If it's such a superior sun filter, you may be wondering why it's taken so long for the FDA to allow it to be sold, but Marcelus assures us it's not because it's unsafe to use.
 "In most of the world, sunscreens are regulated as cosmetics, which is a faster path. In the U.S., the FDA treats sunscreen ingredients like over-the-counter drugs, so they have to clear a much higher bar of testing," she said.
 The current BEMT market is still fairly scant and still growing (one formula literally became available just yesterday!), so check back for the latest bemotrizinol sunscreens to hit U.S. shelves.
 The experts consulted for this story do not endorse the products ahead unless otherwise noted. 
 A weightless milky sunscreen by La Roche-Posay Amazon
 A weightless milky sunscreen by La Roche-Posay
 This lightwieght sunscreen by La Roche-Posay promises to be vastly different from the thick and greasy sunscreens that you might be most used to. Instead, the bemotrizinol-containing formula boasts a thin, milky texture that absorbs instantly into the skin, leaving an invisible finish, while promising lasting hydration and up to 16 hours of antioxidant protection from environmental stressors that can cause skin aging. It uses SPF 50.
 Advertisement Advertisement $40 at Amazon 
 An ultra-sheer sunscreen with peptides and a cloud-like feel Amazon
 An ultra-sheer sunscreen with peptides and a cloud-like feel
 Neutrogena's bemotrizinol sunscreen offers more than just SPF 70 broad-spectrum sun protection. It also features micro-peptides , an anti-aging ingredient known to encourage collagen production for plumper and more hydrated skin. This thin and ultra-sheer formula uses potent antioxidants for even more anti-aging protection and what the brand calls "Cloud-Tech" technology, a type of finish that feels cloud-like and completely weightless on the skin.
 $17 at Amazon 
 $20 at Ulta 
 A bemotrizinol formulated just for acne-prone skin Amazon
 A bemotrizinol formulated just for acne-prone skin
 Just like Neutrogena bemotrizinol sunscreen from above, this lightwieght and white-cast-free formula promises a non-greasy texture and a cloud-like feel, except the finish is more matte, which is suitable for oily and acne-prone skin. The SPF 60 broad-spectrum formula also contains niacinamide, a reliable antioxidant that can calm redness and control excess oil production.
